text:
A muscle fibre relaxes when calcium ions are pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum, causing troponin-tropomyosin to block myosin-binding sites on actin and stopping cross-bridge cycling. The note's claim about a safety mechanism that shuts down contraction at high nerve signal intensity is not correct—stronger stimulation generally increases contraction, and relaxation follows the end of stimulation and calcium reuptake.

CONFIDENCE: 90
